5.outline:
- 5:1 [claim] For every high priest taken from among men is ordained for men in things to God, that he may offer both gifts and sacrifices for sins:
  - 5:2 [--] Who can have compassion on the ignorant, and on them that are out of the way;
    - 5:2 [evidence] for that he himself also is compassed with infirmity.
  - 5:3 [--] And by reason hereof he ought, as for the people, so also for himself, to offer for sins.
  - 5:4 [contrast] And no man taketh this honour unto himself, but he that is called of God, as Aaron.
  - 5:5 [contrast] So also Christ glorified not himself to be made an high priest; but he that said unto him, Thou art my Son, to day have I begotten thee.
    - 5:6 [citation] As he saith also in another, Thou a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec.
  - 5:7 [--] Who in the days of his flesh, when he had offered up prayers and supplications with strong crying and tears unto him that was able to save him from death, and was heard in that he feared;
  - 5:8 [contrast] Though he were a Son, yet learned he obedience by the things which he suffered;
  - 5:9 [--] And being made perfect, he became the author of eternal salvation unto all them that obey him;
  - 5:10 [--] Called of God an high priest after the order of Melchisedec.
- 5:11 [claim] Of whom we have many things to say, and hard to be uttered, seeing ye are dull of hearing.
  - 5:12 [evidence] For when for the time ye ought to be teachers, ye have need that one teach you again which the first principles of the oracles of God; and are become such as have need of milk, and not of strong meat.
  - 5:13 [evidence] For every one that useth milk unskilful in the word of righteousness:
    - 5:13 [evidence] for he is a babe.
  - 5:14 [contrast] But strong meat belongeth to them that are of full age, those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil.

6.outline:
- 6:1 [claim+consequence] Therefore leaving the principles of the doctrine of Christ, let us go on unto perfection; not laying again the foundation of repentance from dead works, and of faith toward God,
  - 6:2 [--] Of the doctrine of baptisms, and of laying on of hands, and of resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment.
  - 6:3 [--] And this will we do, if God permit.
- 6:4 [evidence] For impossible for those who were once enlightened, and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost,
  - 6:5 [--] And have tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the world to come,
  - 6:6 [qualification] If they shall fall away, to renew them again unto repentance; seeing they crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put to an open shame.
- 6:7 [evidence] For the earth which drinketh in the rain that cometh oft upon it, and bringeth forth herbs meet for them by whom it is dressed, receiveth blessing from God:
  - 6:8 [contrast] But that which beareth thorns and briers rejected, and nigh unto cursing; whose end to be burned.
- 6:9 [contrast] But, beloved, we are persuaded better things of you, and things that accompany salvation, though we thus speak.
  - 6:10 [evidence] For God not unrighteous to forget your work and labour of love, which ye have shewed toward his name, in that ye have ministered to the saints, and do minister.
  - 6:11 [--] And we desire that every one of you do shew the same diligence to the full assurance of hope unto the end:
  - 6:12 [purpose] That ye be not slothful, but followers of them who through faith and patience inherit the promises.
- 6:13 [evidence] For when God made promise to Abraham, because he could swear by no greater, he sware by himself,
  - 6:14 [speech] Saying, Surely blessing I will bless thee, and multiplying I will multiply thee.
  - 6:15 [consequence] And so, after he had patiently endured, he obtained the promise.
  - 6:16 [evidence] For men verily swear by the greater: and an oath for confirmation to them an end of all strife.
  - 6:17 [--] Wherein God, willing more abundantly to shew unto the heirs of promise the immutability of his counsel, confirmed by an oath:
  - 6:18 [purpose] That by two immutable things, in which impossible for God to lie, we might have a strong consolation, who have fled for refuge to lay hold upon the hope set before us:
  - 6:19 [--] Which we have as an anchor of the soul, both sure and stedfast, and which entereth into that within the veil;
  - 6:20 [--] Whither the forerunner is for us entered, Jesus, made an high priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec.

7.outline:
- 7:1 [claim] For this Melchisedec, king of Salem, priest of the most high God, who met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings, and blessed him;
  - 7:2 [--] To whom also Abraham gave a tenth part of all;
  - 7:2 [definition] first being by interpretation King of righteousness, and after that also King of Salem, which is, King of peace;
  - 7:3 [--] Without father, without mother, without descent, having neither beginning of days, nor end of life;
  - 7:3 [contrast] but made like unto the Son of God;
  - 7:3 [--] abideth a priest continually.
- 7:4 [claim] Now consider how great this man , unto whom even the patriarch Abraham gave the tenth of the spoils.
- 7:5 [claim] And verily they that are of the sons of Levi, who receive the office of the priesthood, have a commandment to take tithes of the people according to the law, that is, of their brethren, though they come out of the loins of Abraham:
  - 7:6 [contrast] But he whose descent is not counted from them received tithes of Abraham, and blessed him that had the promises.
  - 7:7 [evidence] And without all contradiction the less is blessed of the better.
  - 7:8 [contrast] And here men that die receive tithes; but there he , of whom it is witnessed that he liveth.
  - 7:9 [analogy] And as I may so say, Levi also, who receiveth tithes, payed tithes in Abraham.
  - 7:10 [evidence] For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him.
- 7:11 [claim+qualification] If therefore perfection were by the Levitical priesthood, (for under it the people received the law,) what further need  that another priest should rise after the order of Melchisedec, and not be called after the order of Aaron?
  - 7:12 [evidence] For the priesthood being changed, there is made of necessity a change also of the law.
  - 7:13 [evidence] For he of whom these things are spoken pertaineth to another tribe, of which no man gave attendance at the altar.
  - 7:14 [evidence] For  evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood.
  - 7:15 [contrast] And it is yet far more evident:
    - 7:15 [evidence] for that after the similitude of Melchisedec there ariseth another priest,
    - 7:16 [--] Who is made, not after the law of a carnal commandment, but after the power of an endless life.
    - 7:17 [evidence] For he testifieth, Thou  a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec.
  - 7:18 [evidence] For there is verily a disannulling of the commandment going before for the weakness and unprofitableness thereof.
  - 7:19 [evidence] For the law made nothing perfect, but the bringing in of a better hope ; by the which we draw nigh unto God.
- 7:20 [claim] And inasmuch as not without an oath :
  - 7:21 [evidence] (For those priests were made without an oath; but this with an oath by him that said unto him, The Lord sware and will not repent, Thou  a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec:)
  - 7:22 [consequence] By so much was Jesus made a surety of a better testament.
- 7:23 [claim] And they truly were many priests, because they were not suffered to continue by reason of death:
  - 7:24 [contrast] But this , because he continueth ever, hath an unchangeable priesthood.
  - 7:25 [consequence] Wherefore he is able also to save them to the uttermost that come unto God by him, seeing he ever liveth to make intercession for them.
- 7:26 [claim] For such an high priest became us,  holy, harmless, undefiled, separate from sinners, and made higher than the heavens;
  - 7:27 [--] Who needeth not daily, as those high priests, to offer up sacrifice, first for his own sins, and then for the people's:
    - 7:27 [evidence] for this he did once, when he offered up himself.
  - 7:28 [evidence] For the law maketh men high priests which have infirmity;
  - 7:28 [contrast] but the word of the oath, which was since the law,  the Son, who is consecrated for evermore.

8.outline:
- 8:1 [claim] Now of the things which we have spoken the sum: We have such an high priest, who is set on the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens;
  - 8:2 [--] A minister of the sanctuary, and of the true tabernacle, which the Lord pitched, and not man.
  - 8:3 [evidence] For every high priest is ordained to offer gifts and sacrifices: wherefore of necessity that this man have somewhat also to offer.
  - 8:4 [qualification] For if he were on earth, he should not be a priest, seeing that there are priests that offer gifts according to the law:
  - 8:5 [--] Who serve unto the example and shadow of heavenly things, as Moses was admonished of God when he was about to make the tabernacle: for, See, saith he, thou make all things according to the pattern shewed to thee in the mount.
- 8:6 [claim+contrast] But now hath he obtained a more excellent ministry, by how much also he is the mediator of a better covenant, which was established upon better promises.
- 8:7 [claim+evidence] For if that first had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second.
  - 8:8 [evidence] For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah:
  - 8:9 [contrast] Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord.
  - 8:10 [evidence] For this the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, saith the Lord; I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts: and I will be to them a God, and they shall be to me a people:
  - 8:11 [--] And they shall not teach every man his neighbour, and every man his brother, saying, Know the Lord: for all shall know me, from the least to the greatest.
  - 8:12 [evidence] For I will be merciful to their unrighteousness, and their sins and their iniquities will I remember no more.
- 8:13 [claim] In that he saith, A new, he hath made the first old. Now that which decayeth and waxeth old ready to vanish away.

9.outline:
- 9:1 [claim] Then verily the first had also ordinances of divine service, and a worldly sanctuary.
  - 9:2 [evidence] For there was a tabernacle made; the first, wherein the candlestick, and the table, and the shewbread; which is called the sanctuary.
  - 9:3 [--] And after the second veil, the tabernacle which is called the Holiest of all;
    - 9:4 [--] Which had the golden censer, and the ark of the covenant overlaid round about with gold, wherein the golden pot that had manna, and Aaron's rod that budded, and the tables of the covenant;
    - 9:5 [--] And over it the cherubims of glory shadowing the mercyseat; of which we cannot now speak particularly.
- 9:6 [claim] Now when these things were thus ordained, the priests went always into the first tabernacle, accomplishing the service.
  - 9:7 [contrast] But into the second the high priest alone once every year, not without blood, which he offered for himself, and the errors of the people:
  - 9:8 [evidence] The Holy Ghost this signifying, that the way into the holiest of all was not yet made manifest, while as the first tabernacle was yet standing:
    - 9:9 [--] Which a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience;
    - 9:10 [--] only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed until the time of reformation.
- 9:11 [claim] But Christ being come an high priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this building;
  - 9:12 [contrast] Neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption.
  - 9:13 [evidence] For if the blood of bulls and of goats, and the ashes of an heifer sprinkling the unclean, sanctifieth to the purifying of the flesh:
  - 9:14 [analogy] How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to God, purge your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?
- 9:15 [claim+consequence] And for this cause he is the mediator of the new testament, that by means of death, for the redemption of the transgressions under the first testament, they which are called might receive the promise of eternal inheritance.
  - 9:16 [evidence] For where a testament, there must also of necessity be the death of the testator.
  - 9:17 [evidence] For a testament of force after men are dead: otherwise it is of no strength at all while the testator liveth.
  - 9:18 [--] Whereupon neither the first was dedicated without blood.
    - 9:19 [evidence] For when Moses had spoken every precept to all the people according to the law, he took the blood of calves and of goats, with water, and scarlet wool, and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book, and all the people,
    - 9:20 [speech] Saying, This the blood of the testament which God hath enjoined unto you.
    - 9:21 [--] Moreover he sprinkled with blood both the tabernacle, and all the vessels of the ministry.
    - 9:22 [--] And almost all things are by the law purged with blood; and without shedding of blood is no remission.
- 9:23 [claim+consequence] therefore necessary that the patterns of things in the heavens should be purified with these; but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these.
  - 9:24 [evidence] For Christ is not entered into the holy places made with hands, the figures of the true; but into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God for us:
  - 9:25 [contrast] Nor yet that he should offer himself often, as the high priest entereth into the holy place every year with blood of others;
  - 9:26 [evidence] For then must he often have suffered since the foundation of the world: but now once in the end of the world hath he appeared to put away sin by the sacrifice of himself.
  - 9:27 [analogy] And as it is appointed unto men once to die, but after this the judgment:
  - 9:28 [consequence] So Christ was once offered to bear the sins of many; and unto them that look for him shall he appear the second time without sin unto salvation.

10.outline:
- 10:1 [claim] For the law having a shadow of good things to come, not the very image of the things, can never with those sacrifices which they offered year by year continually make the comers thereunto perfect.
  - 10:2 [evidence] For then would they not have ceased to be offered?
  - 10:2 [evidence] because that the worshippers once purged should have had no more conscience of sins.
- 10:3 [contrast] But in those a remembrance again of sins every year.
- 10:4 [evidence] For not possible that the blood of bulls and of goats should take away sins.
- 10:5 [claim+consequence] Wherefore when he cometh into the world, he saith, Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not, but a body hast thou prepared me:
  - 10:6 [--] In burnt offerings and for sin thou hast had no pleasure.
  - 10:7 [--] Then said I, Lo, I come (in the volume of the book it is written of me,) to do thy will, O God.
- 10:8 [claim] Above when he said, Sacrifice and offering and burnt offerings and for sin thou wouldest not, neither hadst pleasure; which are offered by the law;
- 10:9 [claim] Then said he, Lo, I come to do thy will, O God.
  - 10:9 [--] He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second.
  - 10:10 [--] By the which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once.
- 10:11 [claim] And every priest standeth daily ministering and offering oftentimes the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins:
- 10:12 [contrast] But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God;
  - 10:13 [--] From henceforth expecting till his enemies be made his footstool.
  - 10:14 [evidence] For by one offering he hath perfected for ever them that are sanctified.
- 10:15 [claim] the Holy Ghost also is a witness to us:
  - 10:15 [evidence] for after that he had said before,
  - 10:16 [speech] This the covenant that I will make with them after those days, saith the Lord, I will put my laws into their hearts, and in their minds will I write them;
  - 10:17 [--] And their sins and iniquities will I remember no more.
- 10:18 [claim] Now where remission of these no more offering for sin.
- 10:19 [claim] Having therefore, brethren, boldness to enter into the holiest by the blood of Jesus,
  - 10:20 [--] By a new and living way, which he hath consecrated for us, through the veil, that is to say, his flesh;
  - 10:21 [--] And an high priest over the house of God;
  - 10:22 [--] Let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience, and our bodies washed with pure water.
  - 10:23 [--] Let us hold fast the profession of faith without wavering; (for he faithful that promised;)
  - 10:24 [--] And let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works:
  - 10:25 [--] Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some; but exhorting: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching.
- 10:26 [claim] For if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins,
  - 10:27 [contrast] But a certain fearful looking for of judgment and fiery indignation, which shall devour the adversaries.
  - 10:28 [--] He that despised Moses' law died without mercy under two or three witnesses:
  - 10:29 [--] Of how much sorer punishment, suppose ye, shall he be thought worthy, who hath trodden under foot the Son of God, and hath counted the blood of the covenant, wherewith he was sanctified, an unholy thing, and hath done despite unto the Spirit of grace?
- 10:30 [claim] For we know him that hath said, Vengeance unto me, I will recompense, saith the Lord.
  - 10:30 [--] And again, The Lord shall judge his people.
  - 10:31 [--] a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.
- 10:32 [contrast] But call to remembrance the former days, in which, after ye were illuminated, ye endured a great fight of afflictions;
  - 10:33 [--] Partly, whilst ye were made a gazingstock both by reproaches and afflictions; and partly, whilst ye became companions of them that were so used.
  - 10:34 [evidence] For ye had compassion of me in my bonds, and took joyfully the spoiling of your goods, knowing in yourselves that ye have in heaven a better and an enduring substance.
- 10:35 [claim+consequence] Cast not away therefore your confidence, which hath great recompence of reward.
- 10:36 [evidence] For ye have need of patience, that, after ye have done the will of God, ye might receive the promise.
- 10:37 [evidence] For yet a little while, and he that shall come will come, and will not tarry.
- 10:38 [claim] Now the just shall live by faith:
  - 10:38 [contrast] but if draw back, my soul shall have no pleasure in him.
- 10:39 [contrast] But we are not of them who draw back unto perdition; but of them that believe to the saving of the soul.

11.outline:
- 11:1 [claim] Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.
  - 11:2 [evidence] For by it the elders obtained a good report.
  - 11:3 [evidence] Through faith we understand that the worlds were framed by the word of God,
    - 11:3 [consequence] so that things which are seen were not made of things which do appear.
- 11:4 [claim] By faith Abel offered unto God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain,
  - 11:4 [evidence] by which he obtained witness that he was righteous, God testifying of his gifts:
  - 11:4 [--] and by it he being dead yet speaketh.
- 11:5 [claim] By faith Enoch was translated that he should not see death;
  - 11:5 [--] and was not found,
    - 11:5 [evidence] because God had translated him:
    - 11:5 [evidence] for before his translation he had this testimony, that he pleased God.
- 11:6 [claim+contrast] But without faith  impossible to please :
  - 11:6 [evidence] for he that cometh to God must believe that he is,
  - 11:6 [--] and  he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.
- 11:7 [claim] By faith Noah, being warned of God of things not seen as yet, moved with fear, prepared an ark to the saving of his house;
  - 11:7 [--] by the which he condemned the world,
  - 11:7 [--] and became heir of the righteousness which is by faith.
- 11:8 [claim] By faith Abraham, when he was called to go out into a place which he should after receive for an inheritance, obeyed;
  - 11:8 [--] and he went out, not knowing whither he went.
  - 11:9 [--] By faith he sojourned in the land of promise, as  a strange country, dwelling in tabernacles with Isaac and Jacob, the heirs with him of the same promise:
    - 11:10 [evidence] For he looked for a city which hath foundations, whose builder and maker  God.
- 11:11 [claim] Through faith also Sara herself received strength to conceive seed, and was delivered of a child when she was past age,
  - 11:11 [evidence] because she judged him faithful who had promised.
  - 11:12 [consequence] Therefore sprang there even of one, and him as good as dead,  as the stars of the sky in multitude, and as the sand which is by the sea shore innumerable.
- 11:13 [claim] These all died in faith, not having received the promises,
  - 11:13 [--] but having seen them afar off,
  - 11:13 [--] and were persuaded of ,
  - 11:13 [--] and embraced ,
  - 11:13 [--] and confessed that they were strangers and pilgrims on the earth.
  - 11:14 [evidence] For they that say such things declare plainly that they seek a country.
  - 11:15 [--] And truly, if they had been mindful of that  from whence they came out, they might have had opportunity to have returned.
  - 11:16 [contrast] But now they desire a better , that is, an heavenly:
    - 11:16 [consequence] wherefore God is not ashamed to be called their God:
    - 11:16 [evidence] for he hath prepared for them a city.
- 11:17 [claim] By faith Abraham, when he was tried, offered up Isaac:
  - 11:17 [--] and he that had received the promises offered up his only begotten ,
  - 11:18 [--] Of whom it was said, That in Isaac shall thy seed be called:
  - 11:19 [--] Accounting that God  able to raise  up, even from the dead;
    - 11:19 [--] from whence also he received him in a figure.
- 11:20 [claim] By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau concerning things to come.
- 11:21 [claim] By faith Jacob, when he was a dying, blessed both the sons of Joseph;
  - 11:21 [--] and worshipped,  upon the top of his staff.
- 11:22 [claim] By faith Joseph, when he died, made mention of the departing of the children of Israel;
  - 11:22 [--] and gave commandment concerning his bones.
- 11:23 [claim] By faith Moses, when he was born, was hid three months of his parents,
  - 11:23 [evidence] because they saw  a proper child;
  - 11:23 [--] and they were not afraid of the king's commandment.
- 11:24 [claim] By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter;
  - 11:25 [--] Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season;
  - 11:26 [--] Esteeming the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures in Egypt:
    - 11:26 [evidence] for he had respect unto the recompence of the reward.
  - 11:27 [--] By faith he forsook Egypt, not fearing the wrath of the king:
    - 11:27 [evidence] for he endured, as seeing him who is invisible.
  - 11:28 [--] Through faith he kept the passover, and the sprinkling of blood,
    - 11:28 [purpose] lest he that destroyed the firstborn should touch them.
  - 11:29 [--] By faith they passed through the Red sea as by dry :
    - 11:29 [--] which the Egyptians assaying to do were drowned.
  - 11:30 [--] By faith the walls of Jericho fell down, after they were compassed about seven days.
  - 11:31 [--] By faith the harlot Rahab perished not with them that believed not, when she had received the spies with peace.
- 11:32 [claim+objection] And what shall I more say?
  - 11:32 [evidence] for the time would fail me to tell of Gedeon, and  Barak, and  Samson, and  Jephthae;  David also, and Samuel, and  the prophets:
  - 11:33 [--] Who through faith subdued kingdoms, wrought righteousness, obtained promises, stopped the mouths of lions,
  - 11:34 [--] Quenched the violence of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, out of weakness were made strong, waxed valiant in fight, turned to flight the armies of the aliens.
  - 11:35 [--] Women received their dead raised to life again:
  - 11:35 [--] and others were tortured, not accepting deliverance;
    - 11:35 [purpose] that they might obtain a better resurrection:
  - 11:36 [--] And others had trial of  mockings and scourgings, yea, moreover of bonds and imprisonment:
  - 11:37 [--] They were stoned, they were sawn asunder, were tempted, were slain with the sword:
  - 11:37 [--] they wandered about in sheepskins and goatskins; being destitute, afflicted, tormented;
  - 11:38 [--] (Of whom the world was not worthy:) they wandered in deserts, and  mountains, and  dens and caves of the earth.
  - 11:39 [--] And these all, having obtained a good report through faith, received not the promise:
  - 11:40 [--] God having provided some better thing for us,
    - 11:40 [purpose] that they without us should not be made perfect.

12.outline:
- 12:1 [claim] Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset , and let us run with patience the race that is set before us,
  - 12:2 [--] Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of  faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God.
  - 12:3 [evidence] For consider him that endured such contradiction of sinners against himself, lest ye be wearied and faint in your minds.
  - 12:4 [--] Ye have not yet resisted unto blood, striving against sin.
  - 12:5 [--] And ye have forgotten the exhortation which speaketh unto you as unto children, My son, despise not thou the chastening of the Lord, nor faint when thou art rebuked of him:
    - 12:6 [evidence] For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth.
    - 12:7 [qualification] If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not?
    - 12:8 [contrast] But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons.
    - 12:9 [--] Furthermore we have had fathers of our flesh which corrected , and we gave  reverence: shall we not much rather be in subjection unto the Father of spirits, and live?
      - 12:10 [evidence] For they verily for a few days chastened  after their own pleasure; but he for  profit, that  might be partakers of his holiness.
      - 12:11 [contrast] Now no chastening for the present seemeth to be joyous, but grievous: nevertheless afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness unto them which are exercised thereby.
- 12:12 [claim+consequence] Wherefore lift up the hands which hang down, and the feeble knees;
  - 12:13 [--] And make straight paths for your feet, lest that which is lame be turned out of the way; but let it rather be healed.
  - 12:14 [--] Follow peace with all , and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord:
  - 12:15 [--] Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God; lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble , and thereby many be defiled;
  - 12:16 [--] Lest there  any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright.
    - 12:17 [evidence] For ye know how that afterward, when he would have inherited the blessing, he was rejected: for he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears.
- 12:18 [claim] For ye are not come unto the mount that might be touched, and that burned with fire, nor unto blackness, and darkness, and tempest,
  - 12:19 [--] And the sound of a trumpet, and the voice of words; which  they that heard intreated that the word should not be spoken to them any more:
    - 12:20 [evidence] (For they could not endure that which was commanded, And if so much as a beast touch the mountain, it shall be stoned, or thrust through with a dart:
    - 12:21 [--] And so terrible was the sight,  Moses said, I exceedingly fear and quake:)
  - 12:22 [contrast] But ye are come unto mount Sion, and unto the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to an innumerable company of angels,
    - 12:23 [--] To the general assembly and church of the firstborn, which are written in heaven, and to God the Judge of all, and to the spirits of just men made perfect,
    - 12:24 [--] And to Jesus the mediator of the new covenant, and to the blood of sprinkling, that speaketh better things than  Abel.
- 12:25 [claim] See that ye refuse not him that speaketh. For if they escaped not who refused him that spake on earth, much more  we , if we turn away from him that  from heaven:
  - 12:26 [--] Whose voice then shook the earth: but now he hath promised, saying, Yet once more I shake not the earth only, but also heaven.
  - 12:27 [--] And this , Yet once more, signifieth the removing of those things that are shaken, as of things that are made, that those things which cannot be shaken may remain.
  - 12:28 [consequence] Wherefore we receiving a kingdom which cannot be moved, let us have grace, whereby we may serve God acceptably with reverence and godly fear:
    - 12:29 [evidence] For our God  a consuming fire.

13.outline:
- 13:1 [claim] Let brotherly love continue.
- 13:2 [claim] Be not forgetful to entertain strangers:
  - 13:2 [evidence] for thereby some have entertained angels unawares.
- 13:3 [claim] Remember them that are in bonds, as bound with them;
  - 13:3 [analogy] them which suffer adversity, as being yourselves also in the body.
- 13:4 [claim] Marriage honourable in all, and the bed undefiled:
  - 13:4 [contrast] but whoremongers and adulterers God will judge.
- 13:5 [claim] conversation without covetousness;
  - 13:5 [claim] content with such things as ye have:
    - 13:5 [evidence] for he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee.
- 13:6 [consequence] So that we may boldly say, The Lord my helper, and I will not fear what man shall do unto me.
- 13:7 [claim] Remember them which have the rule over you, who have spoken unto you the word of God:
  - 13:7 [claim] whose faith follow,
    - 13:7 [evidence] considering the end of conversation.
- 13:8 [claim] Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever.
- 13:9 [claim] Be not carried about with divers and strange doctrines.
  - 13:9 [evidence] For a good thing that the heart be established with grace; not with meats, which have not profited them that have been occupied therein.
- 13:10 [claim] We have an altar, whereof they have no right to eat which serve the tabernacle.
- 13:11 [evidence] For the bodies of those beasts, whose blood is brought into the sanctuary by the high priest for sin, are burned without the camp.
- 13:12 [consequence] Wherefore Jesus also, that he might sanctify the people with his own blood, suffered without the gate.
- 13:13 [claim] Let us go forth therefore unto him without the camp, bearing his reproach.
- 13:14 [evidence] For here have we no continuing city,
  - 13:14 [contrast] but we seek one to come.
- 13:15 [claim] By him therefore let us offer the sacrifice of praise to God continually,
  - 13:15 [restatement] that is, the fruit of lips giving thanks to his name.
- 13:16 [contrast] But to do good and to communicate forget not:
  - 13:16 [evidence] for with such sacrifices God is well pleased.
- 13:17 [claim] Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves:
  - 13:17 [evidence] for they watch for your souls, as they that must give account,
    - 13:17 [purpose] that they may do it with joy, and not with grief:
      - 13:17 [evidence] for that unprofitable for you.
- 13:18 [claim] Pray for us:
  - 13:18 [evidence] for we trust we have a good conscience, in all things willing to live honestly.
- 13:19 [contrast] But I beseech the rather to do this,
  - 13:19 [purpose] that I may be restored to you the sooner.
- 13:20 [claim] Now the God of peace, that brought again from the dead our Lord Jesus, that great shepherd of the sheep, through the blood of the everlasting covenant,
- 13:21 [claim] Make you perfect in every good work to do his will, working in you that which is wellpleasing in his sight, through Jesus Christ;
  - 13:21 [claim] to whom glory for ever and ever. Amen.
- 13:22 [claim] And I beseech you, brethren, suffer the word of exhortation:
  - 13:22 [evidence] for I have written a letter unto you in few words.
- 13:23 [claim] Know ye that brother Timothy is set at liberty;
  - 13:23 [qualification] with whom, if he come shortly, I will see you.
- 13:24 [claim] Salute all them that have the rule over you, and all the saints.
  - 13:24 [claim] They of Italy salute you.
- 13:25 [claim] Grace with you all. Amen.

1.outline:
- 1:1 [claim] Paul, an apostle, (not of men, neither by man, but by Jesus Christ, and God the Father, who raised him from the dead;)
  - 1:2 [--] And all the brethren which are with me, unto the churches of Galatia:
  - 1:3 [--] Grace to you and peace from God the Father, and our Lord Jesus Christ,
  - 1:4 [--] Who gave himself for our sins, that he might deliver us from this present evil world, according to the will of God and our Father:
  - 1:5 [--] To whom glory for ever and ever. Amen.
- 1:6 [claim] I marvel that ye are so soon removed from him that called you into the grace of Christ unto another gospel:
  - 1:7 [contrast] Which is not another; but there be some that trouble you, and would pervert the gospel of Christ.
  - 1:8 [contrast] But though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel unto you than that which we have preached unto you, let him be accursed.
  - 1:9 [restatement] As we said before, so say I now again, If any preach any other gospel unto you than that ye have received, let him be accursed.
  - 1:10 [evidence] For do I now persuade men, or God? or do I seek to please men? for if I yet pleased men, I should not be the servant of Christ.
- 1:11 [claim] But I certify you, brethren, that the gospel which was preached of me is not after man.
  - 1:12 [evidence] For I neither received it of man, neither was I taught, but by the revelation of Jesus Christ.
  - 1:13 [evidence] For ye have heard of my conversation in time past in the Jews' religion, how that beyond measure I persecuted the church of God, and wasted it:
  - 1:14 [--] And profited in the Jews' religion above many my equals in mine own nation, being more exceedingly zealous of the traditions of my fathers.
  - 1:15 [contrast] But when it pleased God, who separated me from my mother's womb, and called by his grace,
    - 1:16 [purpose] To reveal his Son in me, that I might preach him among the heathen; immediately I conferred not with flesh and blood:
    - 1:17 [contrast] Neither went I up to Jerusalem to them which were apostles before me; but I went into Arabia, and returned again unto Damascus.
    - 1:18 [--] Then after three years I went up to Jerusalem to see Peter, and abode with him fifteen days.
    - 1:19 [contrast] But other of the apostles saw I none, save James the Lord's brother.
    - 1:20 [--] Now the things which I write unto you, behold, before God, I lie not.
    - 1:21 [--] Afterwards I came into the regions of Syria and Cilicia;
    - 1:22 [--] And was unknown by face unto the churches of Judaea which were in Christ:
    - 1:23 [contrast] But they had heard only, That he which persecuted us in times past now preacheth the faith which once he destroyed.
    - 1:24 [--] And they glorified God in me.

2.outline:
- 2:1 [claim] Then fourteen years after I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, and took Titus with me also.
  - 2:2 [--] And I went up by revelation, and communicated unto them that gospel which I preach among the Gentiles, but privately to them which were of reputation, lest by any means I should run, or had run, in vain.
  - 2:3 [contrast] But neither Titus, who was with me, being a Greek, was compelled to be circumcised:
    - 2:4 [evidence] And that because of false brethren unawares brought in, who came in privily to spy out our liberty which we have in Christ Jesus, that they might bring us into bondage:
    - 2:5 [purpose] To whom we gave place by subjection, no, not for an hour; that the truth of the gospel might continue with you.
  - 2:6 [contrast] But of these who seemed to be somewhat, (whatsoever they were, it maketh no matter to me: God accepteth no man's person:) for they who seemed to be somewhat in conference added nothing to me:
    - 2:7 [contrast] But contrariwise, when they saw that the gospel of the uncircumcision was committed unto me, as the gospel of the circumcision was unto Peter;
      - 2:8 [evidence] (For he that wrought effectually in Peter to the apostleship of the circumcision, the same was mighty in me toward the Gentiles:)
    - 2:9 [--] And when James, Cephas, and John, who seemed to be pillars, perceived the grace that was given unto me, they gave to me and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship; that we should go unto the heathen, and they unto the circumcision.
    - 2:10 [contrast] Only they would that we should remember the poor; the same which I also was forward to do.
- 2:11 [claim] But when Peter was come to Antioch, I withstood him to the face, because he was to be blamed.
  - 2:12 [evidence] For before that certain came from James, he did eat with the Gentiles: but when they were come, he withdrew and separated himself, fearing them which were of the circumcision.
  - 2:13 [--] And the other Jews dissembled likewise with him; insomuch that Barnabas also was carried away with their dissimulation.
  - 2:14 [contrast] But when I saw that they walked not uprightly according to the truth of the gospel, I said unto Peter before them all, If thou, being a Jew, livest after the manner of Gentiles, and not as do the Jews, why compellest thou the Gentiles to live as do the Jews?
- 2:15 [claim] We who are Jews by nature, and not sinners of the Gentiles,
  - 2:16 [--] Knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ, even we have believed in Jesus Christ, that we might be justified by the faith of Christ, and not by the works of the law: for by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified.
  - 2:17 [contrast] But if, while we seek to be justified by Christ, we ourselves also are found sinners, is therefore Christ the minister of sin? God forbid.
    - 2:18 [evidence] For if I build again the things which I destroyed, I make myself a transgressor.
    - 2:19 [evidence] For I through the law am dead to the law, that I might live unto God.
  - 2:20 [--] I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me: and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself for me.
  - 2:21 [contrast] I do not frustrate the grace of God: for if righteousness come by the law, then Christ is dead in vain.

3.outline:
- 3:1 [claim] O foolish Galatians, who hath bewitched you, that ye should not obey the truth, before whose eyes Jesus Christ hath been evidently set forth, crucified among you?
  - 3:2 [--] This only would I learn of you, Received ye the Spirit by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith?
  - 3:3 [--] Are ye so foolish? having begun in the Spirit, are ye now made perfect by the flesh?
  - 3:4 [qualification] Have ye suffered so many things in vain? if yet in vain.
  - 3:5 [--] He therefore that ministereth to you the Spirit, and worketh miracles among you, by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith?
  - 3:6 [analogy] Even as Abraham believed God, and it was accounted to him for righteousness.
  - 3:7 [claim+consequence] Know ye therefore that they which are of faith, the same are the children of Abraham.
  - 3:8 [claim] And the scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the heathen through faith, preached before the gospel unto Abraham, In thee shall all nations be blessed.
  - 3:9 [consequence] So then they which be of faith are blessed with faithful Abraham.
- 3:10 [claim+evidence] For as many as are of the works of the law are under the curse: for it is written, Cursed every one that continueth not in all things which are written in the book of the law to do them.
  - 3:11 [contrast] But that no man is justified by the law in the sight of God, evident: for, The just shall live by faith.
  - 3:12 [contrast] And the law is not of faith: but, The man that doeth them shall live in them.
  - 3:13 [claim+evidence] Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us: for it is written, Cursed every one that hangeth on a tree:
  - 3:14 [purpose] That the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Jesus Christ; that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.
- 3:15 [claim] Brethren, I speak after the manner of men; Though but a man's covenant, yet confirmed, no man disannulleth, or addeth thereto.
  - 3:16 [claim] Now to Abraham and his seed were the promises made. He saith not, And to seeds, as of many; but as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ.
  - 3:17 [claim] And this I say, the covenant, that was confirmed before of God in Christ, the law, which was four hundred and thirty years after, cannot disannul, that it should make the promise of none effect.
  - 3:18 [evidence] For if the inheritance of the law, no more of promise: but God gave to Abraham by promise.
- 3:19 [claim] Wherefore then the law? It was added because of transgressions, till the seed should come to whom the promise was made; ordained by angels in the hand of a mediator.
  - 3:20 [claim] Now a mediator is not of one, but God is one.
  - 3:21 [objection] the law then against the promises of God? God forbid: for if there had been a law given which could have given life, verily righteousness should have been by the law.
  - 3:22 [contrast] But the scripture hath concluded all under sin, that the promise by faith of Jesus Christ might be given to them that believe.
- 3:23 [contrast] But before faith came, we were kept under the law, shut up unto the faith which should afterwards be revealed.
  - 3:24 [consequence] Wherefore the law was our schoolmaster unto Christ, that we might be justified by faith.
  - 3:25 [contrast] But after that faith is come, we are no longer under a schoolmaster.
  - 3:26 [evidence] For ye are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus.
  - 3:27 [evidence] For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ.
  - 3:28 [claim] There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus.
  - 3:29 [claim+qualification] And if ye Christ's, then are ye Abraham's seed, and heirs according to the promise.

4.outline:
- 4:1 [claim] Now I say, the heir, as long as he is a child, differeth nothing from a servant, though he be lord of all;
  - 4:2 [contrast] But is under tutors and governors until the time appointed of the father.
  - 4:3 [analogy] Even so we, when we were children, were in bondage under the elements of the world:
  - 4:4 [contrast] But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law,
  - 4:5 [purpose] To redeem them that were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of sons.
  - 4:6 [evidence] And because ye are sons, God hath sent forth the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father.
  - 4:7 [consequence] Wherefore thou art no more a servant, but a son; and if a son, then an heir of God through Christ.
- 4:8 [claim] Howbeit then, when ye knew not God, ye did service unto them which by nature are no gods.
  - 4:9 [contrast] But now, after that ye have known God, or rather are known of God, how turn ye again to the weak and beggarly elements, whereunto ye desire again to be in bondage?
  - 4:10 [--] Ye observe days, and months, and times, and years.
  - 4:11 [--] I am afraid of you, lest I have bestowed upon you labour in vain.
- 4:12 [claim+address] Brethren, I beseech you, be as I; for I as ye: ye have not injured me at all.
  - 4:13 [--] Ye know how through infirmity of the flesh I preached the gospel unto you at the first.
  - 4:14 [contrast] And my temptation which was in my flesh ye despised not, nor rejected; but received me as an angel of God, as Christ Jesus.
  - 4:15 [objection] Where is then the blessedness ye spake of? for I bear you record, that, if possible, ye would have plucked out your own eyes, and have given them to me.
  - 4:16 [objection] Am I therefore become your enemy, because I tell you the truth?
  - 4:17 [--] They zealously affect you, not well; yea, they would exclude you, that ye might affect them.
  - 4:18 [contrast] But good to be zealously affected always in good, and not only when I am present with you.
  - 4:19 [--] My little children, of whom I travail in birth again until Christ be formed in you,
  - 4:20 [evidence] I desire to be present with you now, and to change my voice; for I stand in doubt of you.
- 4:21 [claim] Tell me, ye that desire to be under the law, do ye not hear the law?
  - 4:22 [evidence] For it is written, that Abraham had two sons, the one by a bondmaid, the other by a freewoman.
  - 4:23 [contrast] But he of the bondwoman was born after the flesh; but he of the freewoman by promise.
  - 4:24 [restatement] Which things are an allegory: for these are the two covenants; the one from the mount Sinai, which gendereth to bondage, which is Agar.
  - 4:25 [evidence] For this Agar is mount Sinai in Arabia, and answereth to Jerusalem which now is, and is in bondage with her children.
  - 4:26 [contrast] But Jerusalem which is above is free, which is the mother of us all.
  - 4:27 [citation] For it is written, Rejoice, barren that bearest not; break forth and cry, thou that travailest not: for the desolate hath many more children than she which hath an husband.
  - 4:28 [analogy] Now we, brethren, as Isaac was, are the children of promise.
  - 4:29 [contrast] But as then he that was born after the flesh persecuted him after the Spirit, even so now.
  - 4:30 [objection] Nevertheless what saith the scripture? Cast out the bondwoman and her son: for the son of the bondwoman shall not be heir with the son of the freewoman.
  - 4:31 [consequence] So then, brethren, we are not children of the bondwoman, but of the free.

5.outline:
- 5:1 [claim+consequence] Stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free, and be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage.
  - 5:2 [--] Behold, I Paul say unto you, that if ye be circumcised, Christ shall profit you nothing.
    - 5:3 [evidence] For I testify again to every man that is circumcised, that he is a debtor to do the whole law.
  - 5:4 [--] Christ is become of no effect unto you, whosoever of you are justified by the law; ye are fallen from grace.
  - 5:5 [evidence] For we through the Spirit wait for the hope of righteousness by faith.
  - 5:6 [evidence] For in Jesus Christ neither circumcision availeth any thing, nor uncircumcision; but faith which worketh by love.
  - 5:7 [--] Ye did run well; who did hinder you that ye should not obey the truth?
  - 5:8 [--] This persuasion not of him that calleth you.
  - 5:9 [--] A little leaven leaveneth the whole lump.
  - 5:10 [--] I have confidence in you through the Lord, that ye will be none otherwise minded: but he that troubleth you shall bear his judgment, whosoever he be.
  - 5:11 [--] And I, brethren, if I yet preach circumcision, why do I yet suffer persecution? then is the offence of the cross ceased.
  - 5:12 [--] I would they were even cut off which trouble you.
- 5:13 [claim+evidence] For, brethren, ye have been called unto liberty; only not liberty for an occasion to the flesh, but by love serve one another.
  - 5:14 [evidence] For all the law is fulfilled in one word, in this; Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.
  - 5:15 [contrast] But if ye bite and devour one another, take heed that ye be not consumed one of another.
- 5:16 [claim+consequence] I say then, Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh.
  - 5:17 [evidence] For the flesh lusteth against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh: and these are contrary the one to the other: so that ye cannot do the things that ye would.
  - 5:18 [contrast] But if ye be led of the Spirit, ye are not under the law.
  - 5:19 [--] Now the works of the flesh are manifest, which are; Adultery, fornication, uncleanness, lasciviousness,
  - 5:20 [--] Idolatry, witchcraft, hatred, variance, emulations, wrath, strife, seditions, heresies,
  - 5:21 [--] Envyings, murders, drunkenness, revellings, and such like: of the which I tell you before, as I have also told in time past, that they which do such things shall not inherit the kingdom of God.
  - 5:22 [contrast] But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith,
  - 5:23 [--] Meekness, temperance: against such there is no law.
  - 5:24 [--] And they that are Christ's have crucified the flesh with the affections and lusts.
  - 5:25 [qualification] If we live in the Spirit, let us also walk in the Spirit.
  - 5:26 [--] Let us not be desirous of vain glory, provoking one another, envying one another.

6.outline:
- 6:1 [claim] Brethren, if a man be overtaken in a fault, ye which are spiritual, restore such an one in the spirit of meekness; considering thyself, lest thou also be tempted.
  - 6:2 [--] Bear ye one another's burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ.
  - 6:3 [evidence] For if a man think himself to be something, when he is nothing, he deceiveth himself.
  - 6:4 [contrast] But let every man prove his own work, and then shall he have rejoicing in himself alone, and not in another.
  - 6:5 [evidence] For every man shall bear his own burden.
- 6:6 [claim] Let him that is taught in the word communicate unto him that teacheth in all good things.
- 6:7 [claim] Be not deceived; God is not mocked: for whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap.
  - 6:8 [evidence] For he that soweth to his flesh shall of the flesh reap corruption; but he that soweth to the Spirit shall of the Spirit reap life everlasting.
  - 6:9 [--] And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not.
  - 6:10 [consequence] As we have therefore opportunity, let us do good unto all, especially unto them who are of the household of faith.
- 6:11 [claim] Ye see how large a letter I have written unto you with mine own hand.
- 6:12 [claim] As many as desire to make a fair shew in the flesh, they constrain you to be circumcised; only lest they should suffer persecution for the cross of Christ.
  - 6:13 [evidence] For neither they themselves who are circumcised keep the law; but desire to have you circumcised, that they may glory in your flesh.
  - 6:14 [contrast] But God forbid that I should glory, save in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom the world is crucified unto me, and I unto the world.
  - 6:15 [evidence] For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision availeth any thing, nor uncircumcision, but a new creature.
  - 6:16 [consequence] And as many as walk according to this rule, peace on them, and mercy, and upon the Israel of God.
- 6:17 [claim] From henceforth let no man trouble me: for I bear in my body the marks of the Lord Jesus.
- 6:18 [claim] Brethren, the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ with your spirit. Amen.

1.outline:
- 1:1 [claim] That which was from the beginning, which we have heard, which we have seen with our eyes, which we have looked upon, and our hands have handled, of the Word of life;
  - 1:2 [evidence] (For the life was manifested, and we have seen, and bear witness, and shew unto you that eternal life, which was with the Father, and was manifested unto us;)
- 1:3 [claim] That which we have seen and heard declare we unto you, that ye also may have fellowship with us: and truly our fellowship is with the Father, and with his Son Jesus Christ.
- 1:4 [claim] And these things write we unto you, that your joy may be full.
- 1:5 [claim] This then is the message which we have heard of him, and declare unto you, that God is light, and in him is no darkness at all.
- 1:6 [qualification] If we say that we have fellowship with him, and walk in darkness, we lie, and do not the truth:
- 1:7 [contrast] But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship one with another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin.
- 1:8 [qualification] If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us.
- 1:9 [qualification] If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
- 1:10 [qualification] If we say that we have not sinned, we make him a liar, and his word is not in us.

2.outline:
- 2:1 [claim] My little children, these things write I unto you, that ye sin not.
  - 2:1 [qualification] And if any man sin, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous:
- 2:2 [claim] And he is the propitiation for our sins:
  - 2:2 [contrast] and not for ours only, but also for the whole world.
- 2:3 [claim] And hereby we do know that we know him,
  - 2:3 [qualification] if we keep his commandments.
- 2:4 [claim] He that saith, I know him, and keepeth not his commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in him.
- 2:5 [contrast] But whoso keepeth his word, in him verily is the love of God perfected:
  - 2:5 [claim] hereby know we that we are in him.
- 2:6 [claim] He that saith he abideth in him ought himself also so to walk, even as he walked.
- 2:7 [claim] Brethren, I write no new commandment unto you, but an old commandment which ye had from the beginning.
  - 2:7 [claim] The old commandment is the word which ye have heard from the beginning.
- 2:8 [claim] Again, a new commandment I write unto you, which thing is true in him and in you:
  - 2:8 [evidence] because the darkness is past, and the true light now shineth.
- 2:9 [claim] He that saith he is in the light, and hateth his brother, is in darkness even until now.
- 2:10 [claim] He that loveth his brother abideth in the light, and there is none occasion of stumbling in him.
- 2:11 [contrast] But he that hateth his brother is in darkness, and walketh in darkness, and knoweth not whither he goeth,
  - 2:11 [evidence] because that darkness hath blinded his eyes.
- 2:12 [claim+address] I write unto you, little children,
  - 2:12 [evidence] because your sins are forgiven you for his name's sake.
- 2:13 [claim+address] I write unto you, fathers,
  - 2:13 [evidence] because ye have known him from the beginning.
- 2:13 [claim+address] I write unto you, young men,
  - 2:13 [evidence] because ye have overcome the wicked one.
- 2:13 [claim+address] I write unto you, little children,
  - 2:13 [evidence] because ye have known the Father.
- 2:14 [claim+address] I have written unto you, fathers,
  - 2:14 [evidence] because ye have known him from the beginning.
- 2:14 [claim+address] I have written unto you, young men,
  - 2:14 [evidence] because ye are strong, and the word of God abideth in you, and ye have overcome the wicked one.
- 2:15 [claim] Love not the world, neither the things in the world.
  - 2:15 [qualification] If any man love the world, the love of the Father is not in him.
- 2:16 [evidence] For all that in the world, the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not of the Father, but is of the world.
- 2:17 [claim] And the world passeth away, and the lust thereof:
  - 2:17 [contrast] but he that doeth the will of God abideth for ever.
- 2:18 [claim+address] Little children, it is the last time:
  - 2:18 [analogy] and as ye have heard that antichrist shall come, even now are there many antichrists;
    - 2:18 [claim] whereby we know that it is the last time.
- 2:19 [claim] They went out from us, but they were not of us;
  - 2:19 [evidence] for if they had been of us, they would have continued with us:
  - 2:19 [contrast] but, that they might be made manifest that they were not all of us.
- 2:20 [contrast] But ye have an unction from the Holy One, and ye know all things.
- 2:21 [claim] I have not written unto you because ye know not the truth,
  - 2:21 [contrast] but because ye know it, and that no lie is of the truth.
- 2:22 [claim] Who is a liar but he that denieth that Jesus is the Christ?
  - 2:22 [claim] He is antichrist, that denieth the Father and the Son.
- 2:23 [claim] Whosoever denieth the Son, the same hath not the Father: .
- 2:24 [claim] Let that therefore abide in you, which ye have heard from the beginning.
  - 2:24 [qualification] If that which ye have heard from the beginning shall remain in you, ye also shall continue in the Son, and in the Father.
- 2:25 [claim] And this is the promise that he hath promised us, eternal life.
- 2:26 [claim] These have I written unto you concerning them that seduce you.
- 2:27 [contrast] But the anointing which ye have received of him abideth in you, and ye need not that any man teach you:
  - 2:27 [contrast] but as the same anointing teacheth you of all things, and is truth, and is no lie, and even as it hath taught you, ye shall abide in him.
- 2:28 [claim+address] And now, little children, abide in him;
  - 2:28 [purpose] that, when he shall appear, we may have confidence, and not be ashamed before him at his coming.
- 2:29 [qualification] If ye know that he is righteous, ye know that every one that doeth righteousness is born of him.

3.outline:
- 3:1 [claim] Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God:
  - 3:1 [consequence] therefore the world knoweth us not,
    - 3:1 [evidence] because it knew him not.
- 3:4 [claim] Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law:
  - 3:4 [evidence] for sin is the transgression of the law.
- 3:11 [claim+evidence] For this is the message that ye heard from the beginning,
  - 3:11 [purpose] that we should love one another.
- 3:16 [claim] Hereby perceive we the love ,
  - 3:16 [evidence] because he laid down his life for us:
  - 3:16 [consequence] and we ought to lay down  lives for the brethren.
- 3:19 [claim] And hereby we know that we are of the truth,
  - 3:19 [consequence] and shall assure our hearts before him.

4.outline:
- 4:1 [claim] Beloved, believe not every spirit, but try the spirits whether they are of God: because many false prophets are gone out into the world.
  - 4:2 [evidence] Hereby know ye the Spirit of God: Every spirit that confesseth that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is of God:
  - 4:3 [contrast] And every spirit that confesseth not that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is not of God: and this is that of antichrist, whereof ye have heard that it should come; and even now already is it in the world.
  - 4:4 [evidence] Ye are of God, little children, and have overcome them: because greater is he that is in you, than he that is in the world.
  - 4:5 [consequence] They are of the world: therefore speak they of the world, and the world heareth them.
  - 4:6 [--] We are of God: he that knoweth God heareth us; he that is not of God heareth not us. Hereby know we the spirit of truth, and the spirit of error.
- 4:7 [claim] Beloved, let us love one another: for love is of God; and every one that loveth is born of God, and knoweth God.
  - 4:8 [evidence] He that loveth not knoweth not God; for God is love.
  - 4:9 [evidence] In this was manifested the love of God toward us, because that God sent his only begotten Son into the world, that we might live through him.
  - 4:10 [contrast] Herein is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us, and sent his Son the propitiation for our sins.
  - 4:11 [qualification] Beloved, if God so loved us, we ought also to love one another.
  - 4:12 [--] No man hath seen God at any time. If we love one another, God dwelleth in us, and his love is perfected in us.
- 4:13 [claim] Hereby know we that we dwell in him, and he in us, because he hath given us of his Spirit.
  - 4:14 [--] And we have seen and do testify that the Father sent the Son the Saviour of the world.
  - 4:15 [--] Whosoever shall confess that Jesus is the Son of God, God dwelleth in him, and he in God.
  - 4:16 [--] And we have known and believed the love that God hath to us. God is love; and he that dwelleth in love dwelleth in God, and God in him.
- 4:17 [claim] Herein is our love made perfect, that we may have boldness in the day of judgment: because as he is, so are we in this world.
  - 4:18 [contrast] There is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear: because fear hath torment. He that feareth is not made perfect in love.
  - 4:19 [--] We love him, because he first loved us.
- 4:20 [claim] If a man say, I love God, and hateth his brother, he is a liar: for he that loveth not his brother whom he hath seen, how can he love God whom he hath not seen?
  - 4:21 [--] And this commandment have we from him, That he who loveth God love his brother also.

5.outline:
- 5:1 [claim] Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God:
  - 5:1 [--] and every one that loveth him that begat loveth him also that is begotten of him.
- 5:2 [claim] By this we know that we love the children of God,
  - 5:2 [qualification] when we love God,
  - 5:2 [--] and keep his commandments.
- 5:3 [evidence] For this is the love of God,
  - 5:3 [--] that we keep his commandments:
  - 5:3 [--] and his commandments are not grievous.
- 5:4 [evidence] For whatsoever is born of God overcometh the world:
  - 5:4 [--] and this is the victory that overcometh the world,
    - 5:4 [--] our faith.
- 5:5 [claim] Who is he that overcometh the world,
  - 5:5 [contrast] but he that believeth that Jesus is the Son of God?
- 5:6 [claim] This is he that came by water and blood, Jesus Christ;
  - 5:6 [contrast] not by water only, but by water and blood.
  - 5:6 [--] And it is the Spirit that beareth witness,
    - 5:6 [evidence] because the Spirit is truth.
- 5:7 [evidence] For there are three that bear record in heaven,
  - 5:7 [--] the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost:
  - 5:7 [--] and these three are one.
- 5:8 [claim] And there are three that bear witness in earth,
  - 5:8 [--] the Spirit, and the water, and the blood:
  - 5:8 [--] and these three agree in one.
- 5:9 [qualification] If we receive the witness of men,
  - 5:9 [claim] the witness of God is greater:
    - 5:9 [evidence] for this is the witness of God which he hath testified of his Son.
- 5:10 [claim] He that believeth on the Son of God hath the witness in himself:
  - 5:10 [contrast] he that believeth not God hath made him a liar;
    - 5:10 [evidence] because he believeth not the record that God gave of his Son.
- 5:11 [claim] And this is the record,
  - 5:11 [--] that God hath given to us eternal life,
  - 5:11 [--] and this life is in his Son.
- 5:12 [claim] He that hath the Son hath life;
  - 5:12 [contrast] he that hath not the Son of God hath not life.
- 5:13 [claim] These things have I written unto you that believe on the name of the Son of God;
  - 5:13 [purpose] that ye may know that ye have eternal life,
  - 5:13 [--] and that ye may believe on the name of the Son of God.
- 5:14 [claim] And this is the confidence that we have in him,
  - 5:14 [qualification] that, if we ask any thing according to his will, he heareth us:
- 5:15 [claim] And if we know that he hear us, whatsoever we ask,
  - 5:15 [--] we know that we have the petitions that we desired of him.
- 5:16 [qualification] If any man see his brother sin a sin not unto death,
  - 5:16 [claim] he shall ask,
    - 5:16 [--] and he shall give him life for them that sin not unto death.
  - 5:16 [claim] There is a sin unto death:
    - 5:16 [--] I do not say that he shall pray for it.
- 5:17 [claim] All unrighteousness is sin:
  - 5:17 [--] and there is a sin not unto death.
- 5:18 [claim] We know that whosoever is born of God sinneth not;
  - 5:18 [contrast] but he that is begotten of God keepeth himself,
  - 5:18 [--] and that wicked one toucheth him not.
- 5:19 [claim] we know that we are of God,
  - 5:19 [--] and the whole world lieth in wickedness.
- 5:20 [claim] And we know that the Son of God is come,
  - 5:20 [--] and hath given us an understanding,
    - 5:20 [purpose] that we may know him that is true,
    - 5:20 [--] and we are in him that is true,
      - 5:20 [--] in his Son Jesus Christ.
  - 5:20 [claim] This is the true God,
  - 5:20 [--] and eternal life.
- 5:21 [claim] Little children, keep yourselves from idols. Amen.
